opening.text: Drive up a hill on a foggy morning. You can't see the top. You can't see the valley below. For a moment, you wonder if the road is even there. But the road hasn't moved. The fog is only in the way. Doubt is often like fog. It hides what is still true.

mainMessage.text: Doubt is fog on the road. The road is still there, and we can keep moving.

blocks.text: **Ask for help** In a fog, we slow down and ask for help. We don't have to face doubt alone.

Behold, I say unto you that whoso believeth in Christ, doubting nothing, whatsoever he shall ask the Father in the name of Christ it shall be granted him; and this promise is unto all, even unto the ends of the earth.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Lord, I Believe” from the April 2013 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
When doubt or difficulty come, do not be afraid to ask for help.
Ask for help.
**Stay near the source of light** Fog is thickest when we turn away from the light. We stay close to God.

And when ye shall receive these things, I would exhort you that ye would ask God, the Eternal Father, in the name of Christ, if these things are not true; and if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost.

President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Lord, I Believe; Help Thou Mine Unbelief” from the October 2003 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Do not let your private doubts separate you from the divine source of knowledge.
Stay near the light.
**Remember the ground you've crossed** In the fog, we remember the miles already driven. What we have already learned is still true.
And I said unto him: I know that he loveth his children; nevertheless, I do not know the meaning of all things.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Lord, I Believe” from the April 2013 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
In moments of fear or doubt or troubling times, hold the ground you have already won, even if that ground is limited.
Hold your ground.
**Faith is part of the road** We don't see all of the road at once. That's why it's called faith.

And now, I, Moroni, would speak somewhat concerning these things; I would show unto the world that faith is things which are hoped for and not seen; wherefore, dispute not because ye see not, for ye receive no witness until after the trial of your faith.

President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Lord, I Believe; Help Thou Mine Unbelief” from the October 2003 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Spiritual knowledge always requires an exercise of faith.
Faith is part of the road.
**Questions are allowed** A driver in fog asks, "Where am I?" That's a smart question. Honest questions are not a sin.

But, behold, I say unto you, that you must study it out in your mind; then you must ask me if it be right, and if it is right I will cause that your bosom shall burn within you; therefore, you shall feel that it is right.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Lord, I Believe” from the April 2013 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Be as candid about your questions as you need to be; life is full of them on one subject or another.
Questions are allowed.
**Keep moving** Fog lifts as we drive. Faith grows as we go forward.

But behold, if ye will awake and arouse your faculties, even to an experiment upon my words, and exercise a particle of faith, yea, even if ye can no more than desire to believe, let this desire work in you, even until ye believe in a manner that ye can give place for a portion of my words.

President James E. Faust, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Lord, I Believe; Help Thou Mine Unbelief” from the October 2003 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
By going forward in faith, you will find that your faith will increase.
Keep going.

story.title: The father who asked for help

blocks.text: A father brought his suffering son to Jesus. He wasn't sure Jesus could help.

Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth. And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
He didn't hide his doubt. He named it and asked for help. And the Lord helped.

application.text: First, write down one honest doubt or question. Second, pray about it, telling Heavenly Father exactly where you are. Third, do one thing you know is true this week, like reading a scripture.

mainMessage.text: Doubt is dust on the window. With care, the view comes back.

blocks.text: **Don't be afraid to ask** We don't need to hide a dusty window. We ask for a cloth.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when something once unclear became clear. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Thomas and the Savior

blocks.text: Thomas said he wouldn't believe until he saw for himself. The Savior came to him.

The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe. Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.
The Savior didn't turn Thomas away. He met him where he was. Thomas ended with a strong witness.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they asked a hard question and found an answer. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: John the Baptist asks a question

blocks.text: John was in prison. He sent his disciples to ask Jesus a plain question.

Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another? Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.
Jesus didn't scold John. He pointed to what was true: the works He was doing. When we're unsure, we can look at what is true too.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they faced a doubt instead of ignoring it. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Gideon asks for a sign

blocks.text: Gideon was told God would use him. He wasn't sure. He said so plainly.

And Gideon said unto him, Oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of, saying, Did not the Lord bring us up from Egypt? but now the Lord hath forsaken us, and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites. And Gideon said unto God, If thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said, Behold, I will put a fleece of wool in the floor; and if the dew be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said.
Gideon brought his honest doubts to God. God was patient with him, and Gideon went on to lead his people.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they stepped out in faith even while unsure. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Peter on the water

blocks.text: Peter stepped out of the boat toward Jesus. Then he looked at the wind.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
Peter did the hardest part. He got out of the boat. When he sank, he called out, and the Savior caught him right away.

application.text: First, pick one act of faith you've been putting off, like prayer, church, or a quiet moment with the scriptures. Second, ask Heavenly Father to be close while you do it. Third, do it this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior catches us when we call. I know faith grows when we step in. I know doubt does not have the last word. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to pick one act of faith you have been putting off, like prayer, church or a quiet moment with the scriptures.
I invite you to ask Heavenly Father to be close while you do it.

blessings: Your faith will grow as you act.
